Right-To-Left Override (RTLO) is a unicode control character that is used to reverse the order of characters in languages that are written from right to left. Attackers can use this character to obscure the true extension of a file, potentially tricking users into executing malicious files. For example, an attacker could rename a malicious executable from "evil.exe" to "evilgpj.[RLO]exe.doc" which would appear as "evilgpjcod.exe" to the user. You can see this write up for [Snapchat here](https://hackerone.com/reports/196222). 

**Verification Requirement:**

_The application should validate and sanitize input to prevent the misuse of unicode control characters such as RTLO (U+202E)._
